2026-10-31.heading: Saint of the Day
2026-10-31.name: Saint Epimachus of Pelusium
2026-10-31.story: The Maronite calendar lists Saint Epimachus on October 31 without details. We have matched this entry to the martyr Epimachus of Pelusium, because the name and the date fit: the Orthodox calendar keeps the Martyr Epimachus of Pelusium, who suffered in Alexandria, on October 31. The Roman Martyrology also keeps Saint Epimachus of Pelusium on October 31: as is handed down, during the persecution of Emperor Decius he saw that the prefect was forcing Christians to sacrifice to idols, tried to overthrow the altar, and was arrested, tortured and finally beheaded by the sword. According to his traditional life, Epimachus lived as an ascetic on Mount Pelusium in Egypt, working as a weaver with his companions Theodore and Callinicos. When he heard that the governor was torturing Christians, he went to El-Bakroug, destroyed some pagan idols and declared that he too was a Christian. He was tortured on the wheel and then beheaded. The Coptic Orthodox Church keeps his feast on 14 Pashons.
2026-10-31.provenance: Brief story based on Wikipedia, the Orthodox calendar at Basilica.ro and the Roman Martyrology (2004). The date follows the Maronite calendar.

2026-11-01.heading: Saint of the Day
2026-11-01.name: Saints Cosmas and Damian
2026-11-01.story: The Maronite calendar lists Saints Cosmas and Damian, martyrs, on November 1 without details. On name and date this entry fits the Byzantine feast of the Unmercenary Physicians Cosmas and Damian, kept on November 1. According to their traditional life, the twin brothers were raised in Christian piety in Asia Minor by their mother, Saint Theodota. Trained as physicians, they healed illnesses of body and soul by the power of prayer and never accepted payment, following the Lord's command, 'Freely have you received, freely give.' The brothers reposed in peace and were buried together at Thereman. The Orthodox Church distinguishes three pairs of saints named Cosmas and Damian; the Western Church keeps the better-known martyr twins on September 26.

2026-11-03.heading: Saint of the Day
2026-11-03.name: Saints Akepsimas, Joseph and Aithalas
2026-11-03.story: The Maronite calendar remembers Saints Akepsimas, Joseph and Aithalas, martyrs of Persia, on November 3. According to their traditional life, Akepsimas was bishop of the Christian community in the Persian city of Naesson, loved by his flock for his ascetic life and tireless pastoral work; Joseph was a priest and Aithalas a deacon. When the emperor Sapor ordered Christian clergy to be sought out and killed, the three were arrested, beaten and held in prison for three years. Brought before the emperor, they refused to worship the pagan gods and confessed their faith in Christ; the aged bishop was beheaded, and the priest and deacon were stoned.

2026-11-04.heading: Saint of the Day
2026-11-04.name: Saints Vitalis and Agricola
2026-11-04.story: The Maronite calendar remembers Saints Vitalis and Agricola on November 4. The Catholic Encyclopedia relates that they were martyred at Bologna about 304 during Diocletian's persecution. Agricola, beloved for his gentleness, converted his servant Vitalis to Christianity, and the two became deeply attached to each other. Vitalis suffered martyrdom first; the persecutors then sought in vain, by tortures and by flattery, to win over Agricola, whom they finally crucified. Saint Ambrose's mention of the two martyrs in an oration is the only authority for their lives.

2026-11-06.heading: Saint of the Day
2026-11-06.name: Saint Paul, Patriarch of Constantinople
2026-11-06.story: The Maronite calendar remembers Saint Paul, Patriarch of Constantinople, on November 6. According to his traditional life, Paul was chosen for the patriarchal throne of Constantinople after the death of Patriarch Alexander, when the Arian heresy had flared up again. He is remembered as a confessor who remained faithful to Christ during the Arian controversy.

2026-11-07.heading: Saint of the Day
2026-11-07.name: Saint Hieron and His Companions
2026-11-07.story: The Maronite calendar remembers Saint Hieron and his companions, the thirty-three martyrs of Melitene, on November 7. According to their traditional life, Hieron was born in Tiana in Cappadocia and raised by a pious mother as a kindly and good Christian. Conscripted under emperors who persecuted Christians, he refused to serve them. At Melitene, Hieron and thirty-two other soldiers refused to offer sacrifice to the pagan gods and openly confessed their faith in Christ; after cruel tortures they were imprisoned and beheaded.
